look_here_first: OLD FIELD THREEAWN (native ANNUAL): look for open, few-spikeleted, wiry BRANCHED panicles with three long awns from one lemma. Then inspect ONE mature intact spikelet: lower and upper GLUMES nearly EQUAL in length (~18–25 mm each, awns excluded), lower glume usually 3–7-VEINED. Purple threeawn is perennial with unequal glumes (lower about half upper), generally one lower-glume vein. Panicle shape and color alone cannot decide.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays and Comal — vouchered in the Texas Hill Country grass flora; Travis — USDA/Rootfast county distribution layer records the species in Travis County.

best_field_traits: First isolate one actual lemma and its three spreading AWN branches; don't mistake three different spikelets for Aristida.
OLD FIELD is an ANNUAL: wiry shoots branch freely and no persistent old perennial basal crown remains.
Best species test: lower and upper glumes of ONE intact mature spikelet are long and nearly EQUAL, typically ~18–25 mm excluding awns; 3–7 lower-glume veins under transmitted light (Kew GrassBase).
Purple threeawn is a PERENNIAL tuft with lower glume about HALF its upper and typically one vein; photograph both glumes to decide.
OPEN airy few-spikelet panicle, cauline leaves and long spreading awns are useful SUPPORT, but purple can also open up.
Churchmouse threeawn has tiny coiled central awn; slimspike has shorter glumes, narrow panicle and uneven short awns (comparison-only).
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use glume relative length and LOWER glume vein count on a mature intact spikelet: A. purpurea has ~6–8 mm lower and ~11–15 mm upper (1-veined lower), while A. oligantha has ~18–25 mm subequal glumes (3–7-veined lower). Confirm a perennial vs annual basal crown; panicle shape and awn color are supporting only.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use glume relative length and LOWER glume vein count on a mature intact spikelet: A. purpurea has ~6–8 mm lower and ~11–15 mm upper (1-veined lower), while A. oligantha has ~18–25 mm subequal glumes (3–7-veined lower). Confirm a perennial vs annual basal crown; panicle shape and awn color are supporting only.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Find rooted plant and ONE entire mature spikelet; measure both glumes WITHOUT their own awn tips, then backlight lower glume.
field_matrix.this_species: OLDFIELD annual; many wiry branches, few widely spaced spikelets; glumes long and nearly EQUAL (~18–25 mm), lower with 3–7 veins.
field_matrix.look_alike: PURPLE perennial dense crown and mostly basal rolled leaves; lower glume about HALF of upper (~6–8 vs 11–15 mm in Kew broad treatment), lower 1-veined.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Subequal long multiveined lower glume + annual base → oldfield. Short lower half-length and 1-veined + persistent tuft → purple. Hold Aristida sp. without macro.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Look at central awn base on an intact mature floret.
field_matrix.this_species: Oldfield has 3 spreading long, roughly equal awns typically 30–70 mm.
field_matrix.look_alike: Churchmouse has very short awns: central ~3–8 mm with a basal spiral, lateral ~1–4 mm.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Short coiled central awn means investigate churchmouse, not oldfield.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare whole panicle shape, glume length and central versus lateral awns.
field_matrix.this_species: Oldfield typically has open sparse branches and long subequal glumes 18–25 mm.
field_matrix.look_alike: Slimspike is annual with relatively contracted head, short glumes (~3–9 mm in Texas regional descriptions) and central awn longer than lateral, no strong central basal spiral.
field_matrix.quick_rule: A narrow compact short-glumed inflorescence with uneven shorter awns needs slimspike comparison.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect awns arising from ONE fertile lemma instead of counting surrounding spikelets.
field_matrix.this_species: Aristida typically has THREE lemma awns.
field_matrix.look_alike: Many muhlys or needlegrasses bear a single awn or none; gramas have characteristic branches of many spikelets.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Enter the Aristida key only after seeing awns on one lemma.

not_reliable_alone: Three awns is GENUS, not species.
Open versus narrow panicle without mature glumes.
Annual appearance from a detached stalk.
Broken lower glume or glume measurements including awn.
Long awn length alone, which overlaps varieties.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Oldfield threeawn — follow the actual awn, then MEASURE
steps: START with the locally stored field and awn photographs, especially the long thin awns against an open panicle. Three spreading awns suggest Aristida, not oligantha by themselves.
CHECK ROOTED ANNUAL BASE: oldfield threeawn branches freely from basal and upper nodes. A loose shoot or an overview without the base cannot demonstrate annual duration.
ON A MATURE ATTACHED SPIKELET isolate BOTH long glumes with 1-mm ruler; Kew gives lower 18–25 mm and approximately equal to upper glume, though treatment variation must be retained.
BACKLIGHT the LOWER glume and count its 3–7 longitudinal nerves. Compare A. purpurea's usually 1-veined shorter lower glume, and retain a variety-aware key.
OPEN the true blade–sheath COLLAR under 20× to photograph the short hair-fringe ligule (~0.5 mm). Do not arrow a stem joint or sheath as a ligule.
FOLLOW one fertile lemma through to its THREE separate awn limbs, then inspect mature callus and lemma with mm scale; visible distant awns or botanical illustration cannot prove a measured lemma.
COMPARE the LOCAL ARCHIVED purple-threeawn photo in the look-alike panel with oldfield's opened branch architecture; the site comparison is now locally hosted and independently labeled OTHER SPECIES.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Three awns alone = genus. Species requires matched lower/upper glume ratio, lower vein count and rooted-life-cycle evidence.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 5 actually photographed local exact-species JPEGs plus 1 public-domain drawing; only photographed anatomical structures count as evidence. USGS flowering awn panel remains externally linked, its server previously timed out. New gallery relink reuses the established locally stored different-species purple-threeawn image; no new oldfield macro or speculative arrow. True glume nerves, precise mm ratio, collar and perennial/annual base are still not documented in a single verified specimen.

field_id_finish_pass.look_here_first: OLD FIELD THREEAWN: verify THREE long spreading awn branches from ONE lemma, then trace the wiry branched ANNUAL to its fibrous base. On ONE intact mature spikelet measure BOTH near-equal long glumes and backlight the 3–7-veined LOWER glume. Three awns alone identify Aristida, not this species.

measured_confirmation.evidence_level: Published botanical treatment ranges; NOT measurements taken from the currently archived photographs.
measured_confirmation.growth_form: Warm-season annual, freely branched wiry culms roughly 15–88 cm (Kew GrassBase); no persistent perennial root crown. Field photos must include the rooted base to prove annual habit.
measured_confirmation.panicle: Open, few-spikeleted panicle approximately 5–14 cm long (Kew GrassBase).
measured_confirmation.ligule_and_collar: TRUE ligule is a fringe of very short hairs about 0.5 mm at the blade–sheath junction (Kew GrassBase). Sheath surface usually glabrous; oral hairs may be absent or present. Do not label surrounding sheath hairs as the ligule.
measured_confirmation.spikelet: ONE fertile floret per spikelet; spikelet body approximately 18–25 mm, excluding the long lemma awns; mature floret disarticulates above persistent glumes (Kew GrassBase).
measured_confirmation.lower_glume: Approximately 18–25 mm, generally nearly equal to upper; characteristically 3–7-veined. Its own terminal awn, if present, is tiny (~0.5 mm in Kew treatment).
measured_confirmation.upper_glume: Approximately 18–25 mm, one-veined; its distinct apical awn may be about 10–15 mm. Do not confuse this GLUME awn with any of the three LEMMA awns.
measured_confirmation.fertile_lemma: Approximately 16–28 mm long, three-veined and somewhat rough above; one floret's lemma bears three terminal awn branches (Kew GrassBase).
measured_confirmation.lemma_awns: Three spreading, usually subequal awn limbs approximately 30–70 mm, arising from ONE fertile lemma; unlike a separate upper-glume awn.
measured_confirmation.callus: Floret callus approximately 1 mm, acute and hairy; confirmation requires an isolated mature floret under magnification.
measured_confirmation.variety_and_photo_limit: These are literature ranges, not specimen measurements. Long awns and open panicle alone are insufficient; purple threeawn has variable varieties and overlapping absolute glume sizes.

lookalikes.split: Persistent PERENNIAL tuft with rolled basal blades; lower glume commonly shorter than upper and usually one-veined. Some varieties have long upper glumes (14–25 mm); compare BOTH glumes and LOWER venation, not absolute upper length.
Much shorter awns with a tightly spiraled central awn base, unlike the long spreading near-equal oldfield lemma awns.
More contracted inflorescence, shorter glumes and often unequal shorter awns; examine a mature isolated floret.

crew_field_sequence: 1. Rooted plant + panicle in one frame: annual fibrous base, branched culms, open few-spikeleted head; show cm scale.
2. At the true blade/sheath junction use 20–40× and 0.5–1 mm calibration to resolve the ~0.5-mm ligule hair fringe.
3. Lay ONE complete mature spikelet on a millimeter scale; isolate and measure lower/upper glumes separately WITHOUT counting glume awns.
4. Backlight LOWER glume and count its 3–7 veins; label only veins actually visible in pixels.
5. Separate the fertile three-veined lemma, record the three 30–70-mm awn limbs and any separate upper-glume awn; photograph the ~1-mm hairy callus.
6. Compare a separately verified rooted A. purpurea and its two glumes at the same scale; if lower veins and life cycle cannot be checked, retain Aristida sp. identification.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Verified exact A. oligantha rooted annual and attached full panicle in one sequence with centimeter ruler.
Source-identified mature lower+upper glume pair, both ~18–25 mm with 1-mm ruler, transmitted-light LOWER 3–7 vein macro at 10–20×.
True ~0.5-mm hair-fringe ligule at opened leaf/sheath collar with 0.5-mm scale and focus-verified hairs.
One detached fertile lemma showing three attached long awn limbs and a distinct upper-glume awn/callus; use ruler and provenance.
Matched A. purpurea comparison showing rooted perennial crown and short 1-veined lower glume at equivalent scale.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Wiry annual with an open, few-spikeleted 5–14 cm panicle
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published culms are roughly 15–88 cm and freely branched. Existing panels show long spreading awns and open flowering stems, but no panel proves a rooted annual base. Three awns alone establish Aristida, not A. oligantha.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE FLOWERING HABIT; ROOTED ANNUAL PHOTO GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE THE ROOTED ANNUAL
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fibrous annual base, not a persistent perennial crown
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow one intact flowering culm down to the roots and photograph its branched stem and base together. The archived stem/junction panel is not a root-crown image; a loose panicle cannot establish life history.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · EXPOSE THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Approximately 0.5 mm fringe of hairs at the inner collar
field_id_short_tiles.details: Open the actual blade–sheath junction under 20–40× with a 0.5–1 mm scale. Kew describes a hair-fringe ligule about 0.5 mm; hairs on the sheath or stem junction are not the ligule. No existing panel proves this measurement.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Both about 18–25 mm; lower glume usually 3–7-veined
field_id_short_tiles.details: On ONE mature spikelet separate the nearly equal lower and upper glumes. Backlight the lower to count 3–7 veins; upper is typically one-veined and may carry its own 10–15 mm awn. These are Kew treatment ranges, not measurements from the historical drawing in panel 3.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SAME-SPIKELET GLUME PAIR AND LOWER VEINS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FOLLOW THREE LEMMA AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma 16–28 mm; three spreading awn limbs 30–70 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: One fertile floret bears a three-veined lemma with THREE long, often subequal awn branches from that lemma. The separate upper-glume awn is not a fourth lemma awn. Existing panels 1 and 5 show gross long-awn architecture, not a measured same-lemma insertion or ~1 mm hairy callus.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED LEMMA, AWN FORK AND CALLUS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT FROM PURPLE THREEAWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Oldfield annual with long nearly equal glumes; purple perennial
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 6 is explicitly OTHER SPECIES: A. purpurea. Purple threeawn commonly has a perennial tuft, a one-veined lower glume shorter than its upper; varieties can overlap in upper-glume length. Compare rooted bases and measured paired glumes, never panicle color or three awns alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE KEY PRESENT; MATCHED SPECIMEN MACROS MISSING
